title: I asked for some Vector Art - I was impressed by the quality
author: Desperate_Horror
selftext:
I wanted to explore using Astra 6.2 to make some Vector art, after being pretty uninspired with both Claude and Neon for the same. I wanted some RPG fantasy style characters with animations, so that is very much what I asked for. The look and animation actually turned out great in my opinion. Then to take it a step further I asked for lighting effects and normal maps. It traced the SVG outlines to generate normal maps and added some lighting options.

Godot scenes/code was auto-generated for the purpose of visualizing what was done.

comments.author: Initial_Plastic_8069
comments.body: this is ebtret tha nthe average Ai outputs imo, but still not by much .

comments.author: Mindless-Ebb2446
comments.body: Did you give it access to any external tool ? Like Inkscape ?

replies.author: Desperate_Horror
replies.body: It had access to all the tools I do, including inkscape.

replies.author: counterclockwisdom
replies.body: Which tools did it use for this? Just Inkscape and a Godot menu? What kind of artistic guidelines or requirements do you have in place? This seems noticeably better than usual for AI.

replies.author: Desperate_Horror
replies.body:
It didn't even use Inkscape, the logs said that the SVG was generated/written via a python script.  The project it generated for preview is in Godot 4.7.2.
I tried the same sort of prompt on Neon and got a so so result, and was pretty unsatisfying.

The prompt use was kind of basic.
"I want some 2D vector art graphics of a hero for a fantasy RPG, it should include idle, walk, run and die animations rigged for Godot."
I added generation of goblins, and the lighting and normal maps later.

comments.author: Mesclandre337
comments.body: Excellent work! I saw that you mentioned you have access to Inkscape. Do you know if GPT 6.2 Astra used that tool?

replies.author: Desperate_Horror
replies.body: From looking at it's actions the SVG's look like they were directly written out using a python script. Doesn't look like inkscape was used at all.

comments.author: CodexPleaseReset
comments.body: Great post! Boy I could really go for an ice cold glass of Inkscape™ right about now

comments.author: Not-a-Clever-UN
comments.body: I know vectors are pure math so ai can do them real well natively in python, so naturally, I must ask, as a matter of my own curiosity and to prove my conjecture, please enlighten me with your answer of my burning question... did you use Inkscape?

replies.author: Desperate_Horror
replies.body: As I mentioned in another comment, no inkscape. It used python and math to generate the SVG files. Then Godot to rig and create the animations and demo app.

replies.author: Not-a-Clever-UN
replies.body: yeah, twice was an accident, rest of us are memeing on the people who kept asking. Algorithm rewards your post with "engagement" so it's not necessarily a bad thing...

replies.author: Desperate_Horror
replies.body: I guess then it was, fail-at-meme-day, for me. :D

replies.author: Not-a-Clever-UN
replies.body: ehh, 13 comments and 32 updoot, not a wild success, but certainly not a failure :D
